newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER SHOWCASE-QUIPS FLY AHEAD OF TOP SPANISH CLASH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-QUIPS FLY AHEAD OF TOP SPANISH CLASH.

text.p: Two of the most colourful personalities in football had been eagerly anticipating this weekend's top clash in Spain -- Barcelona striker Ronaldo and Atletico Madrid owner Jesus Gil.

As it turned out, the Brazilian failed to recover from a stretched muscle and misses the game, but Gil had declared that in any case in defender Juan Lopez he held "the antidote" to the prodigious Ronaldo.
The 20-year-old Brazilian replied by saying what just about everybody else in Spain believes: "Presidents ought to work more and talk less."
But Gil, who is adored by journalists constantly seeking a good quote, failed to take the hint.
"I wouldn't pay four billion pesetas ($31 million) for him if I were mad," said Gil when asked if he was interested in signing the Brazilian, "Not even if he had eight legs."
Always full of surprises, Gil then astonished the Spanish pundits by adding that he has a soft spot for the Brazilian.
"He's like Kung Fu, a model for the young, but at the moment he's just a little grasshopper," said Gil, who seems to have mellowed in the wake of Atletico's league and cup double last season.
Meanwhile, defender Lopez, who was sent off in his last league appearance, turned up to training on Wednesday with a rottweiler dog and a baseball cap bearing the words "no fear."
